question: Can changing population mass alone remove A25 compatible losses while retaining its transfer gain, or does this frozen covariance family require a different structural model?
model: Retain 1/2 full-dictionary mass. Allocate the other half as (1-lambda) local source structure plus lambda empirical-population structure. Cached A25 component densities and evidence determine all scores. Lambda=0 is I, lambda=0.5 is frozen H, lambda=1 is M.
analysis: Diagnose all four condition-by-source-group strata on the original eight pair blocks. Compute nominal pair-block bootstrap intervals at every fixed mass, retain all values, and inspect whether any nonzero mass avoids compatible losses in both groups. Report H gains at steps9-12 and21-24 to locate the tradeoff in observation time. Do not select a fitted mass, tune a target model or treat this retrospective grid as independent confirmation.
controls: Cached endpoints0/0.5/1 must reconstruct I/H/M exactly. A25 profiles, scored seeds and groups must retain the original cohort. If an acceptable nonzero region exists, freeze source-held calibration separately; otherwise close weight-only modifications of this model.
limitations: This diagnoses one empirical archive-mixture covariance family. It is not an impossibility theorem for richer meta-priors, a deployment-frequency estimate or target evidence.
